package_info.why_malicious: The app and its backend ecosystem exhibit multiple critical security vulnerabilities: unencrypted transmission of sensitive PII (including location and credentials), excessive permissions, insecure BLE pairing, and unauthenticated API endpoints allowing account takeover and device manipulation. These behaviors enable remote tracking, account hijacking, and device abuse, putting user privacy and security at severe risk.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /api/dmap-analysis-point-server/v2/insertBaseBurialPointInfoV2 HTTP/1.1
Host: prod.api.app.d-map.cn
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

[{"appVersion":"2.4.1","latitude":"40.*","longitude":"-8.*","imei":"629*","userId":1043065036087934976,...}]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app collects device and user PII (including GPS coordinates, IMEI, userId) and transmits it in plaintext via HTTP POST to a remote server in China, enabling real-time user tracking and PII exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Transmitting precise location and device identifiers to a remote server without user consent or encryption is a major privacy violation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps should only transmit necessary data, with user consent, and always over encrypted channels (HTTPS).
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Fitness apps may sync anonymized location data for activity tracking, but with explicit user consent and strong privacy controls.
key_indicators: Transmission of GPS coordinates and IMEI
Unencrypted HTTP POST to foreign server
No user registration required for data exfiltration

execution_context.file_location: All HTTP(S) requests between app and prod.api.app.d-map.cn

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During runtime, all sensitive API requests (registration, password reset, data sync) are sent over unencrypted HTTP, exposing credentials and PII to network sniffing and MiTM attacks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Failure to use HTTPS for authentication and PII exposes users to credential theft and account hijacking.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: All modern apps must use HTTPS/TLS for any sensitive data transmission.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; transmitting credentials over HTTP is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Credentials and PII in plaintext network traffic

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app allows any client to reset the password for any userId by sending a POST request, with or without authentication, enabling full account takeover.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Lack of authentication and authorization on password reset endpoint allows trivial account hijacking.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Password reset should require proof of identity (token, email, etc.) and never be open to arbitrary requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; password reset must always be authenticated.
key_indicators: No authentication required for password reset
UserId is sufficient to hijack any account

execution_context.file_location: Bluetooth Low Energy GATT pairing process

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Pairing is confirmed by shaking the watch or pressing any button; no timeout or strong authentication.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During BLE pairing, the device allows pairing confirmation via simple hand movement or button press, with no timeout or authentication, enabling trivial unauthorized pairing.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Weak pairing mechanism allows attackers in proximity to easily pair and control the device.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: BLE pairing should require explicit user confirmation and/or secure authentication.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some fitness trackers use simple pairing for user convenience, but with timeouts and user prompts.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Write Command (0x52) to handle 0x0022 with value: 2301093127800360affd6d696e679b (spoof call)
Write Command (0x52) to handle 0x0022 with value: 230109311d01010a01180788015200 (set alarm)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, an attacker can send crafted BLE GATT write commands to the watch to spoof incoming calls or set persistent alarms, causing device disruption and user confusion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unrestricted write access to sensitive BLE characteristics allows remote manipulation of device behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: BLE GATT characteristics controlling calls/alarms should be access-controlled and authenticated.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate app may set alarms or trigger notifications, but only after secure pairing and user consent.
key_indicators: Sensitive BLE GATT handles writable without authentication
Ability to spoof calls and set persistent alarms

attack_chain.action: App collects device and user PII (location, IMEI, userId) and transmits it to remote server in China over unencrypted HTTP.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote tracking and PII exfiltration; enables further attacks if data is intercepted.

attack_chain.action: Attacker intercepts unencrypted network traffic to steal credentials or PII, or performs MiTM to hijack sessions.
Attacker uses password reset API to hijack any account by knowing only the userId.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full account takeover and access to all user data.

attack_chain.action: Attacker pairs with victim's watch using weak BLE pairing (hand movement or button press, no timeout).
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote control of device via BLE.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends crafted BLE GATT write commands to spoof calls or set persistent alarms, disrupting device operation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Denial of service, user confusion, or harassment.

behavioral_signatures: Unencrypted HTTP POSTs containing GPS coordinates, IMEI, and userId to prod.api.app.d-map.cn
Password reset API calls without authentication or with only userId
BLE GATT write commands to sensitive handles (e.g., 0x0022) from unauthorized devices
Frequent BLE pairing attempts with minimal user interaction
file_indicators: Android app requesting excessive permissions (location, contacts, SMS, audio, camera, etc.)
BLE traffic with write commands to 0x0022 handle
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor network traffic from mobile devices for unencrypted HTTP requests to prod.api.app.d-map.cn containing GPS, IMEI, or userId fields. Flag any password reset API calls that lack authentication or are made with only a userId. Analyze BLE traffic for unauthorized pairing attempts and GATT write commands to sensitive handles (e.g., 0x0022). Review installed apps for excessive permissions and known Lenovo Watch X package names.
